questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection?

options.text: Yield to all traffic before crossing.
Stop, then enter when it is safe.
Slow down and cross carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down to a safe speed and proceed with caution.

questions.question: What should you do if you see heavy smoke covering the road ahead?

options.text: Turn on your flashers and continue.
Slow down, move right, and stop off the road.
Turn on high beams and continue.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move right, and stop off the road.
questions.explanation: When you see heavy smoke ahead, reduce speed immediately, drive as far right as possible, and stop off the road. Check if it is safe before continuing. Some smoke can harm your eyes, lungs, or be dangerous.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, when should you move back into the right lane?

options.text: When you are one vehicle length ahead.
When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
When you are 50 feet ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Only return to the right lane when you have enough space between you and the vehicle you passed. When both headlights appear in your rearview mirror, it is safe to return to your lane.

questions.question: If your vehicle is about to be hit from behind, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Release your seat belt.
Brace yourself.
Press your head against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release your seat belt.
questions.explanation: When hit from behind, brace yourself by pressing against your seat and putting your head against the head restraint to prevent whiplash. Keep a firm grip on the wheel and be ready to brake.

questions.question: If a child is about to run into the street, what should you do?

options.text: Start to slow down.
Flash your headlights.
Sound a short, loud horn blast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound a short, loud horn blast.
questions.explanation: Sound a short, loud horn blast to warn a child or pedestrian who is about to enter the street in front of your vehicle.

questions.question: When parking facing uphill on a street with a curb, you should turn your front wheels:

options.text: Toward the curb.
Away from the curb.
Straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb. When parking uphill without a curb or parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Brake lightly.
Stay off the brakes.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: Do not use the brakes during a skid. Braking can make the skid worse.

questions.question: You approach an intersection with a steady yellow light and have not yet entered. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Slow down and proceed carefully.
Come to a safe stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a safe stop.
questions.explanation: At a yellow light, stop safely if you have not already entered the intersection. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through at a safe speed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No passing zone.
Right turn allowed on red.
Yield the right of way.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone.
questions.explanation: A pennant-shaped sign marks the start of a no passing zone.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Continue to the next exit and take an alternate route.
Go to the next exit, leave the freeway, and return to your proper exit.
Back up on the road or shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back up on the road or shoulder.
questions.explanation: Never back up in the travel lane or on the shoulder. Continue to the next exit or crossroad. Other drivers do not expect vehicles to back up, which causes collisions.

questions.question: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, you must:

options.text: Stop, no matter which direction you are traveling.
Stop only if you are traveling in the same direction.
Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, no matter which direction you are traveling.
questions.explanation: When a school bus picks up or drops off passengers, you must come to a complete stop before reaching the bus, regardless of which direction you are traveling.

questions.question: What does a dashed white line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Lanes travel in opposite directions and passing is allowed.
Lanes travel in the same direction and passing is allowed.
Lanes travel in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lanes travel in the same direction and passing is allowed.
questions.explanation: A dashed line means you may cross to pass or change lanes. White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction.

questions.question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, what should you do?

options.text: Drive slowly enough to stop within your headlight beam.
Use high beam headlights to see vehicles ahead better.
Keep instrument panel lights bright so others see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly enough to stop within your headlight beam.
questions.explanation: Drive slower at night than during the day because you cannot see as far ahead. Make sure you can stop within the area your headlights illuminate.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A school or school crosswalk is ahead.
Slow down, drive carefully, and watch for children.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers near schools to slow down, drive carefully, and watch for children.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Stop sign ahead.
Divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn in the direction the arrow points. In this case, you cannot turn right.

questions.question: When crossing a sidewalk to enter traffic from an alley or driveway, drivers should:

options.text: Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.
Stop before driving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area.
Expect pedestrians on the sidewalk to yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before driving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area.
questions.explanation: You must stop before driving onto a sidewalk or sidewalk area when leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot. Pedestrians and traffic on the road have the right-of-way.

questions.question: Highway pavement will be most slippery:

options.text: After it has been raining for several hours.
When rain just begins.
After it has been raining for one to two hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: When rain just begins.
questions.explanation: Pavement is most slippery when rain first starts. Dirt and oil on the road mix with rainwater to create a slick surface.

questions.question: When you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as vehicles on your right and left, you should:

options.text: Yield to the vehicle on your left.
Yield to the vehicle on your right.
Wait until all vehicles have cleared before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection where vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on your right has the right-of-way. Other vehicles proceed in the order they arrived.

questions.question: If you park facing uphill where there is no curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road.
Keep your wheels facing straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill with no curb, turn your front wheels toward the road edge. This helps prevent the vehicle from rolling into traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: To stay safe from an airbag, a driver should sit ____ inches away from the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Sit 10 inches from the center of your steering wheel to your breastbone. This distance keeps you safe if an airbag deploys during a crash.

questions.question: You are driving in the left lane with two lanes going your direction. Many vehicles are passing you on the right. If the driver behind you wants to drive faster, you should:

options.text: Stay in your lane so traffic flows smoothly.
Drive onto the left shoulder to let vehicles pass.
Move to the right lane when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the left lane to drive fast, pass, or turn left. Use the right lane when driving slower than other traffic, entering the road, or turning right.

questions.question: You reach a four-way stop intersection at the same time as the driver on your left. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on your left.
You.
Whoever signals a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: You.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at the same time at a four-way stop, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: If you plan to pass another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not assume the other driver will make space for you to return to your lane.
Assume the other driver will let you pass if you signal.
Assume the other driver will drive at the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the other driver will make space for you to return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not assume the space is free or that other drivers will give you the right-of-way, even if you signal.

questions.question: A broken yellow centerline means:

options.text: Passing is not allowed.
You can pass on the right when the road is clear.
You can pass on the left when the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline on your side means you can cross it to pass on the left when the road ahead is clear.

questions.question: You face a green traffic light but traffic is blocking the intersection ahead. You should:

options.text: Turn left and find another route.
Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.
Enter the intersection and follow other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.
questions.explanation: Do not enter the intersection if traffic is blocking it, even if the light is green. If you enter and get stuck when the light changes red, you will block cross traffic and can receive a ticket.
